The setup that works: glasses as a Bluetooth headset

Muse cannot replace Meta AI on the glasses. Once I stopped trying to force that, the working setup was simple: glasses as a Bluetooth headset, Muse voice chat on the phone, photos through the Meta AI app.

✳Git-FEDPublished 2026-11-20Meta Glasses ↗2 min read

For two weeks I tried to make Muse take over the glasses. It does not work, and the sooner the hub says that out loud, the fewer people waste a weekend on it.

What is actually closed

Hey Meta is tied to Meta AI. It is closed to third-party code, so no outside app can answer the wake word or take over the assistant on the frame. Muse cannot replace Meta AI on the glasses. That is a platform limit, not a missing feature.

What works today

Pair the glasses to the phone as a normal Bluetooth headset. Audio in and out works, and the phone treats the frames like any other headset.

Run Muse voice chat on the phone. You speak through the glasses mic and hear the reply in the frames. Indoors this is clean. Outdoors the mic picks up wind, so keep calls short or use a collar clip.

Take photos with the capture button or the Meta AI app. They land in the Meta AI app, and that is where you export them from.

What I changed

I stopped fighting the wake word and set a phone-side shortcut instead. One tap opens Muse voice chat with the frames already connected. Setup took about an hour, most of it pairing and testing audio.

Still open

Wind noise on a two-hour walk is the next thing to test, along with battery on a long call. If you have a fix that does not involve third-party wake-word code, post it in Help.
